n10.F3f.why: CORRECT: The candidate identifies the same feature and comparison as the key — it notes the Blank trace shows prominent ZHSH (♣ = Zn4SO4(OH)6·4H2O) peaks, while the NH4OAc trace lacks this low-angle ♣ cluster and shows mainly Zn peaks, i.e., the insoluble ZHSH by-product is absent with NH4OAc but present in Blank, matching the key's stated finding.

o11.F3f.why: CORRECT: the candidate independently identifies the same features as the key — a low-angle/mid-range cluster of ZHSH-type peaks (♣, Zn4SO4(OH)6·4H2O) concentrated in the Blank trace (matching the key's "~8.5 and 15-35 deg" ZHSH reflections marking the blank-cycled Zn pattern), and the NH4OAc trace dominated by Zn (#) peaks resembling the Bare Zn pattern (matching the key's "NH4OAc pattern is dominated by Zn reflections like bare Zn"). No contradiction with the key.

o12.F3f.why: WRONG: The key states the NH4OAc-cycled Zn pattern still shows a ZHSH (Zn4SO4(OH)6·4H2O) marker on a weak ~8.5° peak, i.e., the phase is still present, just weak. The candidate instead describes the NH4OAc trace as "lacking the strong low-angle ♣ cluster" and peaks "marked mainly with #" (Zn only), concluding the additive "suppressed/altered formation" of the ZHSH phase — i.e., asserting absence rather than a weak-but-present marker. This contradicts the key's central claim that the marker persists (is still detectable) under NH4OAc treatment.

n19.F3h.why: CORRECT: the candidate identifies "This work" at cumulative plated capacity ~5 Ah cm⁻² with Coulombic efficiency ~99.7%, positioned in the upper-right (best-performing) region relative to other reported Zn anode studies, matching the key's claim that this performance is among the best reported. Note current density 10 mA cm-2 is also implied via color scale, consistent with the key.
